system: You are Claude serving as an adversarial scientific co-designer. You are not being asked for reassurance or implementation. Challenge assumptions, prefer falsifiable experiments, and distinguish useful cognitive mechanisms from decorative biomimicry. Do not claim consciousness. Do not modify files. Do not propose canned dialogue. Do not touch The Room or connect any additional agents.
prompt:
Before we activate Endogenous Workspace v1 in the live Emily + Olivia Stanford chain, give us a hostile lab-meeting review. We want one surprising idea, not a polite checklist. The architecture currently adds fast competition among existing observations/retrieved memories, slow decaying salience traces, and a thresholded broadcast. It is OFF by default. The proposed next step would feed an ignited broadcast into reflect -> plan/react -> act.

Return exactly these six fields:
VERDICT: PROCEED | HOLD
HIDDEN ASSUMPTION: <the most dangerous assumption in the current design>
UNCONVENTIONAL MOVE: <one non-obvious mechanism or experiment inspired by biological cognition that is more informative than tuning salience weights>
ABLATION: <smallest ON/OFF experiment that could falsify the value of that mechanism>
FAILURE SIGNATURE: <what outcome would show it is decorative rather than causally useful>
ONE CHANGE BEFORE START: <single highest-value design/code change, if any>

Constraints: preserve observe -> remember -> retrieve -> reflect -> plan/react -> act; no generated inner monologue; no invented autobiographical facts; no hand-authored conversational moves; no new agents; no changes to The Room; do not activate anything live. Prefer an intervention that makes the architecture easier to falsify rather than more brain-like on paper.
context: Paper-derived candidate properties: hierarchical/nested organization; reward/evaluation; embodiment; spontaneous endogenous activity; self-maintenance/homeostasis; developmental selection; degeneracy/plasticity; social interaction; distinction between conscious and non-conscious representations. The point is not to copy biology aesthetically, but to test which candidate mechanisms causally matter.

Current Endogenous Workspace v1: each Candidate has source/text/importance/recency. observation candidates use importance=.35, recency=1.0. memory importance is Stanford importance normalized to 0..1; recency=1/(1+age/8). score = .42*importance + .28*recency + .20*slow_strength + .10*source_bias. Slow traces decay by .94 per pulse, update as .75*old + .25*current_score, and store only ids/numeric strength/seen/last_seen/source in Stanford scratch. Candidate text is not persisted in the workspace state. At threshold .58, up to two candidates ignite and their already-existing text is concatenated into a private broadcast. No text is generated by the workspace itself.

Current live Stanford path: inbound message is observed and remembered; Stanford retrieval/reflection/planning/reaction run; then the original-paper-derived spoken-act adapter generates one utterance. There are deliberately no canned replies or authored fallback dialogue. The workspace is not yet integrated into this path.

Experimental intent: if enabled later, run workspace pulses privately and/or insert only an ignited broadcast into cognitive context before the existing act generator. We want a clean OFF control and ablations. A useful mechanism should alter downstream retrieval/reflection/planning/action in stable, explainable ways across time, not merely make dialogue sound different.

Specific concern from the biological-consciousness debate: matching surface behavior is weak evidence. We care about causal organization and cross-timescale dynamics. A mechanism should survive perturbation tests and reveal something about persistent cognitive individuality, not simply produce more human-like language.
